items.strategy_title: Grid reduction destroys parallelism on high-wave kernels
items.strategy_description: Reducing grid to 660 blocks collapsed occupancy from 91.86% to 30.99%. Only apply when waves_per_sm < 2.

items.strategy_title: Fuse multi-pass reduction into online algorithm
items.strategy_description: 3-pass → 2-pass online softmax. Eliminated global memory round-trip, improved IPC 3.22→3.37.
items.applicable_when: Multi-pass reduction with intermediate global memory writes

items.strategy_description: num_warps 4→8 changed block 128→256, doubled waves, halved DRAM. num_warps controls block size with cascading effects.
items.do_not_apply_when: Occupancy already >90% and waves_per_sm is high

items.strategy_title: Eliminate second pass when row fits in one block
items.strategy_description: When BLOCK_SIZE >= n_cols, entire row fits in registers. One load, one store. Halved memory traffic, 20.7% speedup.
items.applicable_when: BLOCK_SIZE >= n_cols (row fits in one tile)

items.strategy_title: Reduce num_warps to halve block size for DRAM throughput
items.strategy_description: Reducing num_warps from 4 to 2 changed compiled block size from 128 to 64 threads. Despite occupancy dropping 90%→55% and No Eligible rising 30%→54%, DRAM throughput jumped 48%→60% and wall-clock time improved 20.5%. The smaller block size allowed more blocks per SM, improving memory coalescing and L2 utilization. Combined with exp2 and reciprocal multiplication for instruction fusion. This is counterintuitive — the kernel got faster despite worse occupancy because it became more memory-efficient.
items.slow_pseudocode:
# num_warps=4 → block=(128,1,1), 18 regs, 90% occupancy, 105 ns
softmax_kernel[grid](..., num_warps=4, num_stages=1)
exp_vals = tl.exp(vals - row_max)
normalized = exp_vals / row_sum
items.fast_pseudocode:
# num_warps=2 → block=(64,1,1), 21 regs, 55% occupancy, 84 ns
softmax_kernel[grid](..., num_warps=2, num_stages=2)
exp_vals = tl.math.exp2((vals - row_max) * LOG2E)
normalized = exp_vals * (1.0 / row_sum)
items.applicable_when: Memory-bound kernel (Memory Throughput > SM Throughput) with high No Eligible stalls (>25%). When DRAM throughput is below 60% and the block size can be reduced without killing parallelism (waves_per_sm stays > 10).
items.do_not_apply_when: Compute-bound kernels where occupancy is critical for latency hiding. Also avoid if register pressure increases to the point of spilling (check Local Memory Spilling Requests).
items.framework_notes: Triton: num_warps directly controls threads_per_block = num_warps * 32. Reducing from 4→2 halves the block. The effect on register allocation is non-linear — profile to confirm. CUDA equivalent: reduce blockDim.

items.strategy_title: Process 2 rows per program for mild improvement
items.strategy_description: Processing 2 consecutive rows per program (grid halved to 65536) improved occupancy 90%→94% and gave 1.6% speedup. Modest but safe — waves/SM went from 62 to 31, still highly parallel.
items.applicable_when: Grid size >> SM_COUNT * blocks_per_SM and memory-bound. Processing 2-4 rows amortizes setup cost.
items.do_not_apply_when: Do not combine with num_warps reduction — they have opposing effects on block-level parallelism.
